messages.text: For a Wireless Communication use case involving Wi-Fi 7/8, where would Signaling / Non-signaling Tester fit in the test workflow?

In a Wi‑Fi 7/8 wireless communication test workflow, **Signaling / Non-signaling Testers fit mainly at the RF/device test stages**, with different roles depending on whether you need realistic protocol behavior or fast RF measurement.

| Workflow stage | Where the tester fits | Typical role |
|---|---|---|
| **R&D / design bring-up** | **Signaling tester** — e.g., CMX500 | Emulates real-world WLAN operation so engineers can test RF TX/RX, antenna behavior, multi-link operation, coexistence, end-to-end/IP behavior, and multi-radio scenarios under signaling conditions. The knowledge base states that Wi‑Fi 7 development requires RF TX/RX and antenna measurements “under real-world conditions in signaling mode,” and that CMX500 supports Wi‑Fi 7/8 WLAN in a single multi-technology setup. |
| **Feature / performance validation** | **Signaling tester + OTA/chamber setup** | Used for realistic performance assessment, especially for Wi‑Fi 7 features such as MLO, 2x2 MIMO, 6 GHz operation, coexistence, and end-to-end testing. Evidence also mentions CMX500 combined with OTA chambers for assessing Wi‑Fi 7 device performance. |
| **Pre-production / production test development** | **Non-signaling tester** — e.g., CMP180 | Used to validate RF waveforms and optimize fast test sequences before mass production. The knowledge base notes CMP180 can verify wide-band WLAN waveforms, including 480 MHz loopback as a potential Wi‑Fi 8 candidate, and is positioned for R&D and production. |
| **High-volume manufacturing** | **Non-signaling tester** | This is the main fit for non-signaling mode. Production RF measurements are performed in non-signaling mode “to save time,” with CMP180 optimized for this purpose. Wireless Manufacturing Test software is also described as tailored for high-volume production and non-signaling R&D. |
| **Field / QA / troubleshooting** | Evidence insufficient in the KB | The retrieved evidence did not specifically describe field/QA workflows for Wi‑Fi 7/8 signaling/non-signaling testers. In general, not from the KB, signaling mode would be useful for reproducing real connection issues, while non-signaling mode would be useful for quick RF checks. |

**Simple positioning:**  
- Use a **signaling tester** when you need the DUT to behave like it is connected to a real Wi‑Fi/network environment. This is strongest in **R&D, validation, OTA, coexistence, MLO, and end-to-end tests**.  
- Use a **non-signaling tester** when you need fast, repeatable RF measurements without full protocol connection overhead. This is strongest in **manufacturing and production test**, and also useful for non-signaling R&D.

Grounded sources include R&S Wi‑Fi 7/8 CMX500 and CMP180 press materials, including:  
- “Rohde & Schwarz and Broadcom showcase first Wi‑Fi 8 RF signaling tests…”  
- “Rohde & Schwarz presents its Wi‑Fi 7 multi-channel single-box test solutions for R&D and production at MWC 2024”  
- “Bluetest and Rohde & Schwarz collaborate to offer over-the-air testing of next-generation WLAN devices”  
- “EMITE and Rohde & Schwarz join forces to support OTA measurements on Wi‑Fi 7 and 5G RedCap”

answer.question: For a Wireless Communication use case involving Wi-Fi 7/8, where would a Signaling / Non-signaling Tester fit in the test workflow? Include how it is used across R&D, validation, manufacturing, and field/QA if evidence exists.

passages.text: The CMX500 is a modular, powerful one-box signaling tester enabling comprehensive multi-technology testing. It covers LTE and NR in SA/NSA modes, NR-NTN, NB-NTN, Direct-to-Cell (D2C/DTC) testing and WLAN including Wi‑Fi 7 and Wi‑Fi 8. Consequently, the CMX500 allows R&D engineers of wireless devices to comprehensively test their design’s operation in both cellular and non-cellular standards of the latest generation in a single instrument setup.

passages.text: Rohde & Schwarz will display its [R&S CMX500](https://www.rohde-schwarz.com/us/products/test-and-measurement/wireless-tester-network-emulator/cmx500-5g-one-box-signaling-tester_63493-601282.html "CMX500") multi-technology multi-channel signaling tester at MWC 2024 with newly added Wi-Fi 7 testing capabilities. With this functionality, the one-box tester allows R&D engineers of wireless devices to comprehensively test their design’s operation in cellular and non-cellular standards of the latest generation in a single instrument setup. In addition to this, the [R&S CMP180](https://www.rohde-schwarz.com/us/products/test-and-measurement/wireless-tester-rf-analyzer-generator/cmp180-radio-communication-tester_63493-1081280.html "CMP180") radio communication tester will verify a signal waveform of 480 MHz bandwidth in loopback mode, attesting to be a future-proof solution for users in R&D and production, even beyond the requirements of Wi-Fi 7.

passages.text: During the development of WLAN devices, measurements of the RF TX and RX characteristics must be conducted under real-world conditions in signaling mode. The R&S CMX500 one-box tester is a multi-technology multi-channel signaling tester that is now available with integrated Wi-Fi 7 test functionality. Especially in Wi-Fi 7 where Multi-Link-Operation (MLO) is a key feature, a test environment that provides multiple RF chains is crucial. The tester's flexibility, support for multiple radio technologies, and embedded IP test capabilities make it a versatile solution for a wide range of Wi-Fi 7-specific tests, such as 2x2 MIMO, 6 GHz band with out-of-band discovery, coexistence and E2E test capabilities.

passages.text: In the production phase of WLAN devices, all RF measurements are performed in non-signaling mode to save time. Rohde & Schwarz has optimized the [R&S CMP180](https://www.rohde-schwarz.com/us/products/test-and-measurement/wireless-tester-rf-analyzer-generator/cmp180-radio-communication-tester_63493-1081280.html "CMP180") radio communication tester for this purpose. The instrument supports many cellular and non-cellular technologies including Wi-Fi 6E, Wi-Fi 7 and 5G NR FR1 up to 8 GHz in frequency with bandwidths up to 500 MHz. Leveraging the wide bandwidth, the R&S CMP180 will demonstrate at MWC its ability to verify a WLAN waveform with 480 MHz bandwidth in loopback mode, a potential waveform candidate for the yet-to-be-defined Wi-Fi 8 (IEEE 802.11bn) standard. This feature shows that the cost-effective instrument is future-proof for users not only in production, but also in R&D.

passages.text: [Wi-Fi 8](https://www.rohde-schwarz.com/us/solutions/wireless-communications-testing/wireless-standards/wlan-wi-fi/wi-fi-8-testing/wi-fi-8-testing_258504.html "Wi-Fi 8") builds upon the foundation of Wi-Fi 7, retaining core physical layer parameters like supported frequencies up to 7.125 GHz, channel bandwidths up to 320 MHz and 4096QAM modulation, as well as Multi-Link-Operation (MLO). However, to achieve its UHR goals, IEEE 802.11bn introduces a suite of innovative PHY and MAC layer technologies that present new testing hurdles. At MWC 2026, visitors can experience how to address key testing challenges associated with Wi-Fi 8 with the enhanced testing capabilities of the CMX500 one-box signaling tester, one of the most versatile mobile device test platforms in the market, which supports many of the demanding features of Wi-Fi 7 and Wi-Fi 8 today.

passages.text: EMITE’s state-of-the-art over-the-air chambers can now be combined with the latest sophisticated testing features of the [R&S CMX500](https://www.rohde-schwarz.com/us/products/test-and-measurement/wireless-tester-network-emulator/cmx500-5g-one-box-signaling-tester_63493-601282.html "CMX500") one-box signaling tester from Rohde & Schwarz. The radio communication tester offers a wide range of device testing capabilities, supporting cellular technologies such as LTE, 5G NR FR1 frequency range up to 8 GHz and FR2 millimeter wave frequency range up to 50 GHz, including the latest 5G RedCap technology. It also supports non-cellular technologies, including the latest Wi-Fi 7, all in a single instrument. As a consequence of this collaboration, EMITE’s customers obtain a comprehensive environment for accurately assessing the performance of Wi-Fi 7 as well as 5G Red Cap devices.

answer.text:
R&D/development: the CMX500 signaling tester fits early WLAN device testing under real-world signaling mode for antenna and RF TX/RX measurements, including Wi‑Fi 7 MLO tests [5].
R&D for Wi‑Fi 7/8: the CMX500 lets engineers test cellular and non-cellular operation, including WLAN with Wi‑Fi 7 and Wi‑Fi 8, in one setup [1].
Validation/performance assessment: CMX500 with EMITE OTA chambers provides a comprehensive environment for accurately assessing Wi‑Fi 7 device performance [7].
Manufacturing/production: RF measurements are performed in non-signaling mode to save time, with the CMP180 optimized for this purpose [4].
Production and non-signaling R&D: Wireless Manufacturing Test software is tailored for high-volume production testing and non-signaling R&D applications [8].
Wi‑Fi 8 readiness: the CMP180 can verify a 480 MHz WLAN waveform in loopback mode as a potential Wi‑Fi 8 waveform candidate [4].
